title: Playing on advertising wagons
summary: He describes the horse- or mule-drawn advertising wagons and where each musician sat.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. On the wagons, did you ever play on the wagons?
Yeah, I played on the wagons several times. Yeah. We used to have a lot of fun playing on the advertising wagons.
How big a wagon was that? Was it a great big thing like a truck or were they fairly crowded when you got on?

It would be crowded because we hardly ever had the chances to get a big enough thing, you know, and they'd have six of us on there and most of the musicians sitting up in the front, they'd have to all be sitting down, you see, because sometime we'd play while the truck, mostly a mule pulling it. Yeah. Yeah, a horse or mule pulling that thing at that time, you know, a horse or a mule. Later on while we started with a truck, but on this beginning I'm talking about way back there, they had the mule or horse, one of the two was pulling, sometimes two, you know, two horses or two mules would be pulling this wagon, the big wagon, and we'd be piling, playing the bass man and the drum player would always be on the tailgate on the back, on the back playing the tailgate part, see.
You had the whole drum set, snare drum and bass and all?
Yeah, he had the whole deal up there, oh yeah, he had the whole deal up there. Where would the bass be?
Bass on the tailgate.
He's mostly on the tailgate. When he gets ready to knock off, he stands up on the tailgate, you see, and he plays right on the, he's peg on the tailgate.
Peg right out on the tailgate. Where would the trombone be?
The trombone, he's right next to the, right next to the back of the bass man, right by him, you know, up in front of him, but right in the back of him.
The trombone didn't always sit on the tailgate when he was on the tailgate?
Yeah, that's right, yeah, yeah, he did, right on the tailgate. He mostly, he mostly played, you know, out from the tailgate, the trombone man. That's right, yeah, yeah.
Then the clarinet and the clarinet were up in front of him.
That's right, they'd be up in the front, yeah.
Did anybody sit up in the driver's seat or you all sat in back? None of the musicians sat in back?
No, no, no, the musicians couldn't sit in the driver's seat, he had to stay on the, in the truck.
I thought there might be room for two up there if it was close by.
Yeah, but how could he play? He had to play. He couldn't play his instrument if he sat in the front. No. He'd have to sit, uh.
When he rode around, I thought maybe he'd sit up there sometime.
No, no, he'd always stayed there until we'd go around and end the load and then we'd all get off. That's the way, yeah.
